headline: Diesel breaks $6.50 as Ukraine hits Moscow refinery, Trump presses for a halt
intro: Diesel's record run finally hit some resistance this morning, selling off hard after weeks of "diesel diesel diesel" headlines — even as Ukraine's largest overnight drone barrage yet slammed another Russian refinery and Washington leaned on Kyiv to stand down.
overview: Spot diesel sits at $5.338/gal with a $117.18/bbl crack, and retail diesel above $6.28 nationally as truckers, farmers and shippers absorb record costs; gasoline is comparatively calm at $3.535 spot and a $41.45 crack. The diesel spike is increasingly geopolitical: Ukrainian strikes on Moscow-area and Ufa refineries, a Saudi pipeline scare, and Strait of Hormuz risk are all colliding with tight US inventories, prompting Trump to publicly urge Zelenskyy to halt refinery strikes and Congress to pass new Russia-oil tariff authority. On the policy side, California signed its E15 cleanup bill and SAF investment continues apace (Infinium's mSAF platform, OMV Petrom's Petrobrazi project, UK mandate volumes doubling) even as airlines push back on SAF mandate costs.

decks.title: 10-Q (filed 2026-09-18)
decks.analysis:
## Fuel-Segment Takeaways

- **Fuel sales surged on price, not volume**: Supermarket fuel sales rose 25.6% in Q2 2026 ($4,105M vs. $3,269M) and 23.1% for the first two quarters ($9,367M vs. $7,609M), driven almost entirely by average retail fuel price increases of 25.3% (Q2) and 23.9% (YTD) rather than gallon growth.

- **Fuel remains a drag on margin mix**: Management explicitly notes fuel sales "have a very low FIFO gross margin rate" and "very low OG&A rate" compared to non-fuel sales — increased fuel sales mechanically lowered both consolidated gross margin (22.4% vs. 22.5% Q2) and OG&A rate (17.2% vs. 17.6% Q2), a mix effect rather than a fuel-margin deterioration signal.

- **Fuel contributed positively to operating profit**: Increased fuel operating profit was cited as a factor boosting operating profit as % of sales for the first two quarters of 2026 (+18 bps), and higher fuel earnings helped drive YTD adjusted EPS growth (+6%).

- **Identical sales metrics exclude fuel**: All core identical-sales reporting (0.2% Q2, 0.6% YTD) strips out fuel entirely, reflecting continued volatility/distortion from fuel pricing in comparable-sales analysis.

- **No station-count or fuel-center-specific disclosures**: The filing provides no data on number of fuel centers, fuel gallons sold, or membership/loyalty-linked fuel discount dynamics (e.g., fuel points redemption trends).

**Signal for fuels markets**: Kroger's results reflect fuel retail price inflation (~24-25% YoY) flowing through to a major U.S. supermarket fuel retailer's topline, with fuel-related earnings functioning as a modest tailwind to profitability even as fuel's inherently thin margins dilute blended retailer profitability ratios.
